prerequisites: Meeting the enrolment conditions for the Master's study programme of Mechanical Engineering - Research and Development program.

learning_outcomes.text: Have thorough theoretical, methodological and analytical knowledge with elements of a research work that form a basis for very demanding professional work.
Master very demanding and complex work processes and methodological tools in specialised professional fields.
Be able of planning and managing of the working process based on creative solving of problems that are linked to the teaching and training content.
Be able of unique innovations and critical reflections.

syllabus_topics: Socio-economic aspects of energy supply for modern society
Technological aspects of energy supply for modern society (structure of primary energy sources, grid balancing, technologies available)
Transformation of energy supply towards sustainable solutions (RES, circular economy, sectoral coupling, digitalization)
Critical evaluation of technological solutions in terms of environmental indicators
Critical evaluation of technological solutions in terms of energy efficiency
Critical evaluation of technological solutions in terms of basic economic feasibility
Thermodynamic optimization of thermodynamic cycles and applications
Classical thermal power plants (steam, gas, combined, ORC, CHP…)
Integration of distributed energy sources (PV- and wind power plants) into the electricity grids
bibliography: Strauß K.: Kraftwerkstechnik, zur Nutzung fossiler, nuklearer und regenerativer Energiequellen, Springer, 2009
Kopanos G.M., Liu P., Georgiadis M.C.: Advances in Energy Systems Engineering, Springer, 2017
degree: Mechanical Engineering (2nd cycle, Erasmus+ subjects, Research and Development programme)
